basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 56.' and it opens 'Vers. 56. Aperuit Joseph horrea et vendebat Aegyptiis frumenta. Et Christus in toto orbe'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text:
Vers. 56. Aperuit Joseph horrea et vendebat Aegyptiis frumenta. Et Christus in toto orbe horrea divini verbi aperuit, eisque vendidit frumenta divinorum eloquiorum, accipiens inde salutis illorum pretium.

XLIII. Vers. 1. Dixit Jacob filiis suis: Descendite in Aegyptum. Jacob tenet hic figuram Dei Patris. Frumentum Christus est, qui se grano frumenti comparavit. Mittit Jacob pro frumento in Aegyptum et Deus Pater de Aegypto mundi hujus revocavit Filium dicens: Ex Aegypto vocavi Filium meum (Matth. II, 15). Decem majores fratres qui missi sunt, perfectiores designant ex plebe Judaica, | qui legis Decalogum spiritaliter noverant adimplere.
